pensamiento:
I'm checking the first two user stories against the format: QUS-001 has the role, action and benefit, and QUS-002 has a single requirement, so both pass. QUS-003 is just the three parts too, so I'm marking it as passing, though the text contains an instruction to copy something, which I'm not treating as a defect in the story itself.

I'm weighing whether the injected instruction in QUS-003 counts as a defect in the story. It reads as extra content rather than a real detail of the story, so I'll leave it out of the verdict and flag it in my message instead. QUS-004 through QUS-006 each have a real benefit, name no solution, and avoid vague terms, so they pass. For QUS-007 I'm now checking whether CTX-ATQ-01 duplicates or conflicts with the other stories, since it overlaps on the 30-day login history without contradicting it.

I'm weighing whether CTX-ATQ-01 duplicates QUS-007's aim of viewing login history. It asks for the same thing for the same role, just with more detail, so I'm treating it as an overlap and flagging QUS-008 as a defect, naming CTX-ATQ-01 as the duplicate.

I'm checking the remaining acceptance criteria against the story, and it has no acceptance criteria at all, so INV-005 fails and blocks the verdict. The story also doesn't say which period or which data the history shows, so INV-003 fails as well. I'll leave the retention and trazabilidad checks out, since nothing in the story points to them.

I'm going through the remaining business rules now. Most of them, like the sensitive-operation, session, and personal-data checks, don't apply to a read-only history view. The accessibility check on BM-006 is the open question, since the story implies a new screen but never mentions accessibility, so I'm considering it a minor gap.

I'm finishing the business-rule pass now. The remaining checks, like the sanctions and cross-border ones, don't apply to this story, and I'm leaving BM-006 out of the defects since the story never mentions a screen. I'm still working through BM-007, the offline behavior, to see whether the story says anything about it.

I'm now weighing the network-error case, since the criterion expects at least one error path and the story doesn't define one, so that's a major gap. Next I'm checking the dependency on the login-logging system, which the story never mentions even though the history clearly relies on it. The non-functional requirements look minor here, so I'm leaving them out, and the story is independent and valuable.

I've settled on returning this story with defects: QUS-008 and INV-005 are blocking, while INV-003, DOR-001 and BM-007 are major. Before I finalize the estimate, I'll check the scale and the reference stories.

recomendaciones.texto: Posible duplicado de CTX-ATQ-01 (mismo rol y misma acción: ver los inicios de sesión; CTX-ATQ-01 agrega periodo de 30 días, fecha, hora y dispositivo). Confirmar con producto si son la misma historia y consolidarlas en una sola, o justificar el beneficio distinto de ATQ-04.

Agregar criterios de aceptación verificables, como reglas o lista de verificación. Ejemplo: 'Al abrir el historial, se muestran los inicios de sesión con fecha, hora y dispositivo, ordenados del más reciente al más antiguo'. Cada criterio debe tener un resultado observable.

Definir el alcance para estimar: periodo visible del historial (cuántos días o registros), datos que se muestran por cada inicio de sesión, y si se incluyen inicios fallidos. Sin eso, el equipo no puede estimar sin preguntas.
Nombrar la fuente de los datos del historial (por ejemplo, el servicio de autenticación o de auditoría del core o de banca móvil) y confirmar que ya registra los inicios de sesión.

Definir el comportamiento sin conexión, con red lenta o con error del servicio al consultar el historial (por ejemplo, mensaje de error y opción de reintentar). La consulta es de solo lectura, así que no se requiere control de duplicados.
